title: Migrate GetGameLogTool from client-side chat accumulation to server-side bridge events
description:
The bridge accumulates game log text from CHATMESSAGE passive callbacks in a client-side StringBuilder (gameLog). This is the last major passive state dependency in BridgeCallbackHandler after the passive-state audit (minimize-bridge-passive-callback-state).

The server already provides a structured bridge events API (GamePlay.getBridgeEvents → BridgeLogEntry records) with cursor support. GetGameHistoryTool already uses this API. GetGameLogTool should be migrated to use server-side bridge events too, which would eliminate:

1. **gameLog accumulation** from CHATMESSAGE: the 5MB StringBuilder buffer, trimming logic, and gameLogTrimmedChars offset tracking
2. **Turn message rewriting**: currently transforms raw 'TURN X for Player (lives)' into 'Player turn N (lives)' at write time using playerTurnCounts. Could move to the server or be computed at read time from bridge events which already carry turn/activePlayer fields
3. **playerTurnCounts tracking**: HashMap tracking per-player turn counts, only needed for turn rewriting

The migration would also need to address:
- **GetGameLogTool text format**: bridge events are structured records (~12 event types), not free-form text. The text log currently includes more verbose descriptions. Consider whether the structured format is sufficient or whether the server needs to provide richer text.
- **unseenChat system messages**: spell cancellation messages like '[System] Spell cancelled — mana plan was incorrect' are constructed bridge-side and added only to unseenChat, never to gameLog. These need a server-side path or an alternative delivery mechanism.
- **Chat message buffering**: player-to-player TALK messages are buffered in unseenChat and surfaced via attachUnseenChat(). If the server synced recent chat at decision time, this could also move server-side.

After this migration, the only remaining CHATMESSAGE effect would be playerDead detection (parsing chat for '{name} has lost the game').
